speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether the Government can provide updates on (i) the progress of the framework for the equitable sharing of losses suffered by scam victims and (ii) the work of the Payments Council in reviewing the practices that the financial industry can put in place to better protect consumers from scams; and (b) what are current and upcoming efforts of Project Frontier and the Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams on combating scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS is finalising the framework, in coordination with other Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is taking us longer than expected to design a fair and effective framework that ensures shared responsibility across the ecosystem as well as incentives for each party to be vigilant against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS aims to seek public comments on the framework as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: At the broader level, the Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams (IMCS), chaired by the Ministry of Home Affairs, also partners the financial institutions closely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes Project FRONTIER, as mentioned by the Member, where the Police have established processes with financial institutions to swiftly freeze bank accounts suspected of being used in scams, in order to mitigate victims’ losses and disrupt scammers’ operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The IMCS has also strengthened enforcement against perpetrators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Other than enforcement actions, the IMCS has expanded its public education campaign, called "Spot the Signs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Stop the Crimes", to build public awareness and vigilance on how to spot scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, it has shared materials advising the public to not share personal details, such as log-in credentials and one-time-passwords, with unverified parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: IMCS will continue to work with all stakeholders to deepen its public outreach.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is in relation to the loss-sharing framework that the Minister of State shared.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have residents who came up to me to highlight about some of their loss-sharing issues.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I was wondering whether the Minister of State can share how fast this can be rolled out because it has a direct impact on residents in monetary terms.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Two, in relation to the knowledge of contact information for scams, I have a few residents who came up to me experiencing a scam in process while they are literally speaking to a scammer, called 999 but was informed that that is not the number to call.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I was wondering whether more can be done via Project FRONTIER to ensure that there is some coordination between the Police and the banks to handle such situations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I hope the Minister of State can share a bit more on that front in terms of coordination and whether Project FRONTIER can, together with IMCS, actually enhance that.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But we continue to work on this at a very urgent pace.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We understand that this is urgent work and what we are trying to do is to make sure that this loss-sharing and accountability approach incorporates as well as involves all key parties in the ecosystem and every single aspect of this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Every stakeholder has to be vigilant in their own right against scams, both institutions as well as individuals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is why, in my original answer, I said that it was important for all of us to also conduct public outreach and also for the financial institutions and authorities to play their part.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: What we are trying to achieve is, as I mentioned, a fair as well as effective framework so that there is shared responsibility across the ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the Member's residents, this is something that is very important for us to bear in mind.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If members of the public face this issue, they should notify their banks immediately, if they suspect that they are victims of scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Many of the financial institutions, in fact, the major retail banks, have made it easier for the public to report scams by either having dedicated hotline numbers or making it the first few options on their phone banking menu.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, members of the public are encouraged to obtain such hotline numbers from the official sources, such as at the back of the ATM cards and to also save the numbers on their mobile phones.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition, members of the public can also file a Police report either online or in person if they have lost money to scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They can call the anti-scam hotline at 1800 722 6688 for advice.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is managed by both the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) and also the latest ScamShield app that is available now on both android as well as IOS can also be used to report suspicious scam messages.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But, in concert, all of these are also a work in progress.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We also encourage members of the public to give us feedback and also the financial institutions as well as the retail banks on how to tighten this further as we continue to fight as an ecosystem against scams.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have raised PQs on this topic before.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we will factor those into our discussions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But we will take into account the Member's feedback.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will allow one last supplementary question because we need to move on to dengue.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know some banks do it, some banks do not, but I wonder if there is actually a regulation, practice or policy regarding this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But I wonder what the interim recourse is for the scam victims.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have a resident, for example, who lost his life savings of almost a quarter million dollars and he did the right thing – make a Police report, wrote to the authorities, wrote to the banks and so forth, but still extremely distraught and distressed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I wonder what is the recourse for victims like this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think many of our residents have also shared with regard to the scams and one of the issues with regard to banks as well as the scams is on individual responsibility as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But we also make sure that we have constant updates with the Police and will also inform customers on how to report to the Police.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I know that this issue with regard to scams is a rather new one because of the online as well as technology.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But what we are trying to do with both the loss-sharing framework as well as the public outreach to individuals and also to encourage the banks to have good processes in place will be very important for us to manage this issue in a fair and equitable way.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But that notwithstanding, we want to encourage all members of the public to, first, be extremely vigilant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If you see any of these funds being transferred outside, that is, unusual transactions, please inform your banks immediately.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We, on the MAS front, are coordinating very closely with the Police as well as the financial institutions to tighten these processes and this consultation will come in due time so that we can tighten these processes and combat scams together.
